questions.question: Which statement best describes document.querySelector()?
options: It selects all elements that match a CSS selector and returns a NodeList.
It selects the first element that matches a CSS selector and returns that element.
It selects an element only by its id and returns that element.
It selects elements only by their tag name and returns an array.
questions.explanation: document.querySelector() returns the first element in the document that matches the given CSS selector.

questions.question: You want to select all elements with the class todo-item. Which method is the best choice?
questions.explanation: document.querySelectorAll('.todo-item') returns a static NodeList of all elements matching the CSS selector .todo-item.

questions.question: What is a correct way to select a single element with id main-form?
questions.explanation: Using document.querySelector('#main-form') selects the first element in the document with id="main-form".

questions.question: Which value for the position argument of insertAdjacentHTML will insert HTML before the element itself (as a sibling)?
questions.explanation: The 'beforebegin' position inserts HTML immediately before the element, as a sibling in the DOM tree.

questions.question: Given <input type="text" id="username">, which JavaScript line correctly reads the current text that the user typed?
questions.explanation: Form controls store their current text in the value property, not textContent or innerHTML.

questions.question: In a form submit event handler, why do we often call event.preventDefault()?
options: To stop all JavaScript on the page from running.
To prevent the browser from submitting the form and reloading the page.
To clear all inputs in the form automatically.
To permanently disable the submit button.
questions.explanation: event.preventDefault() stops the browser's default submit behavior, allowing you to handle the data in JavaScript instead of doing a full page reload.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to attach a click event handler to a button with id save-btn using JavaScript?
questions.explanation: addEventListener is the recommended pattern because it cleanly attaches handlers, allows multiple listeners, and separates behavior from markup.

questions.question: Which of the following is an inline event handler defined in HTML?
questions.explanation: An inline handler is defined directly in the HTML attribute, such as onclick="submitForm()".

questions.question: Which of these is a good reason to prefer addEventListener over inline event attributes like onclick?
options: Inline handlers are not supported in modern browsers.
addEventListener allows attaching multiple handlers to the same event on the same element.
addEventListener only works for forms, making code shorter.
Inline handlers always run slower than addEventListener.
questions.explanation: addEventListener supports multiple handlers on the same element and keeps JavaScript separate from HTML, improving maintainability.
